title: 5 Dividend Stocks to Watch as Markets Swing on Inflation Fears
content:
U.S. markets were volatile, as geopolitical tensions and oil price swings weighed on sentiment, while strong earnings and economic data provided support. Major indexes fluctuated as investors reacted to tensions in the Middle East, particularly around the Strait of Hormuz, which drove sharp swings in crude oil prices. Sentiment was further pressured by uncertainty surrounding stalled diplomatic efforts.

However, the fundamentals of the U.S. economy remained solid, with consumer confidence at 92.8 in April, Q1 GDP growth at 2%, and manufacturing activity, as reported by the Institute for Supply Management, unchanged at 52.7 in April, indicating continued expansion. Despite this resilience, inflation data showed mixed signals, with headline PCE rising 0.7% in March while core PCE moderated to 0.3%. Meanwhile, a divided Federal Reserve stance and elevated energy costs kept uncertainty alive. Overall, the U.S. economy appears stable in the near term, supported by consumer strength and corporate performance, though geopolitical risks and inflation remain key variables for market direction.

Cautious investors can diversify their portfolios and pick dividend-paying stocks. Some of the prominent names are: FactSet Research SystemsFDS, Cabot CBT, Diamondback Energy FANG, Piper Sandler Companies PIPR and Sturm, Ruger & Company RGR. Companies that pay out dividends consistently indicate a healthy business model. Stocks that have raised dividends recently exhibit a sound financial structure and can counter market upheavals. Moreover, stocks that tend to reward investors with a high dividend payout outperform non-dividend-paying entities in a highly volatile market.

title: Diamondback Energy Lifts Production Guidance After Strong Q1
content:
Diamondback Energy announced its first-quarter 2026 financial and operating results, highlighting average oil production of 521 thousand barrels per day and significant capital returns to shareholders.

Net cash provided by operating activities reached $1.8 billion, with operating cash flow before working capital changes at $2.6 billion. Adjusted EBITDA attributable to Diamondback totaled $2.7 billion, supporting free cash flow of $1.7 billion. The company returned $859 million to shareholders through $548 million in share repurchases and a base dividend raised to $1.10 per share, a 10% increase year over year.

Production averaged 521 MBO/d of oil and 979 MBOE/d overall, driven by strong Midland Basin activity. The company drilled 118 gross wells and completed 147, with net figures of 111 and 137, respectively, across key zones including Wolfcamp and Spraberry. Realized oil prices stood at $73.47 per barrel, with total cash operating costs of $11.26 per BOE.

Full-year 2026 oil production guidance increased to 520 MBO/d from 500-510 MBO/d, with total production at 972 MBOE/d, reflecting 5% organic growth. Cash capital expenditures rose to $3.9 billion, and Q2 oil guidance set at 515-525 MBO/d. Average lateral lengths are projected at 12,900 feet.

Diamondback repurchased 3.3 million shares at a weighted average price of $167.61, with $2.1 billion remaining in authorization. It also completed a tender offer retiring $777 million in senior notes and fully repaid its $550 million term loan, reducing pro forma gross debt to $12.7 billion.

These results underscore Diamondback's operational efficiency and disciplined capital approach in the Permian Basin. With substantial free cash flow generation and a focus on debt reduction, the company positions itself for sustained growth amid market volatility.

By Charles Kennedy for Oilprice.com
